result.summary: Round limit reached, so no files were edited. I agree with both minor findings and checked each. F1: the memo overstates "FCT unsupported". The 1996 speech does support the FCT's existence by 1996, and the memo itself quotes that passage at lines 105 and 122. What lacks primary support is the creation instrument, designation date, component areas and capital-transfer date. F2: my sandbox fetch of the UT index returned HTTP 200 and the page lists the 1993 map, so the memo's "not opened" is out of date for the index page. The map image itself still has not been inspected.

responses.evidence: Memo line 105 and line 122 already quote the speech's '30-state structure with a Federal Capital Territory'. Yet lines 12, 126 and 19 say the FCT is 'not supported' or 'Unsupported by primary text', and line 33 says Source 2 supports nothing for the FCT. The first two are too broad. The accurate claim is that the 1996 speech supports the FCT's existence by 1996. Unsupported by any opened primary text: the FCT creation instrument (Decree No. 6 of 1976 is only a secondary snippet), the designation date, the component areas and parent states, and the 1991 capital-transfer date.
responses.action_taken: No edit (round limit). I recommend the maintainer or a later round qualify lines 19 and 126 along those lines.

responses.evidence: Memo line 88 says 'Opened? No' and that the 1993 listing could not be confirmed. I ran curl against https://maps.lib.utexas.edu/maps/nigeria.html in this session and got HTTP 200. The HTML contains 'The following maps were produced by the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency, unless otherwise indicated.' It also lists 'Nigeria (Political) 1993' as africa/nigeria_pol93.jpg and africa/nigeria_pol_1993.pdf, plus a 1993 shaded-relief map. Not checked: the map image or PDF contents, whether it shows 30 states plus the FCT, and item-specific reuse rights. The CIA attribution is the index page's claim.
responses.action_taken: No edit (round limit). I recommend the memo record that the index page is confirmed, with the listing and CIA attribution, while the map image and its rights stay unchecked.
